lessons.name: Select the sentence that tells about the past

header.text: <instructions>Which sentence tells about the past?</instructions>

choices.text: We will give the squirrels some peanuts.
We will give the squirrels some peanuts.

header.text: <instructions>Which sentence tells about the past?</instructions>

choices.text: We will give the squirrels some peanuts.
We will give the squirrels some peanuts.

header.text: Some verbs tell about something that has already happened. These verbs tell about the past. They usually end in -ed.
Some verbs tell about something that is happening now. These verbs tell about the present. They usually have no ending, or they end in -s.
Some verbs tell about something that is going to happen. These verbs tell about the future. They use the word will.

sentences.text: We will walk to the park next week.

header.text: Look at the verb in each sentence. Which one tells about the past?

sentences.text: The baby pulled his hat off.
The verb pulled ends in -ed. It tells about something that has already happened. It tells about the past. This is the right answer.
We will give the squirrels some peanuts.
The verb will give has the word will. It tells about something that is going to happen. It tells about the future.

header.text: <instructions>Which sentence tells about the past?</instructions>

choices.text: Mr. Green's dog barked at a loud sound.
Mr. Green's dog barked at a loud sound.
Mr. Green's dog barked at a loud sound.
